note: Decides, page by page, whether a page continues the previous page's document. Tiered, not a flat vote: tier 1 is printed pagination and decides on its own; tier 2 is repeated page furniture (patient banner, footer template) and document identity tokens; tier 3 is structure (a title opens a document, a signature closes one). Sentence-level continuity is deliberately absent: on the labelled corpus 'previous page ends without punctuation' scored 28% on continuations vs 29% on new documents. Header and footer bands come from line positions in the Final2 (then Final1) OCR JSON; a page without them falls back to its first and last lines of text. Weights were re-tuned on 80 pagination-labelled page pairs from four charts (55 continuations, 25 new documents), counting a wrong merge three times worse than a wrong split, because a merged page takes the first page's page type and DOS. Reloads on change.

pagination.comment: Tier 1. Requires the word 'page' (or 'pg') so a date like 26/24 is not page 26 of 24. Searched only in the header and footer bands. max_total is page_arbitration.json's max_document_pages: a counter whose total is above it numbers a whole export or fax (60306165: 'of 40' across several documents), not one document, and is ignored.

bands.comment: Where the header and footer are. With line positions: a line whose top is above head_top is header, one whose bottom is below foot_bottom is footer (fractions of page height). Without: the first head_lines and last foot_lines lines of text, and a quarter of the lines each way for pagination.

fingerprint.comment: Tier 2. A line repeating verbatim in the header of consecutive pages fired on 75% of continuations but also on 28% of new documents (separate documents from one EMR share the patient banner), so on its own it does not reach continue_at.

identity.comment: Tier 2. A shared accession or order number is near-proof. A shared MRN only says same patient, which inside one chart is almost always true. None fired on the four tuning charts, so these are the original weights.

structure.comment: Tier 3. A matched section header near the top of the page is a title. A signature on the previous page closes it. These vote rather than decide: a page can carry a title mid-document, or a signature that is not the document's own.

decision.comment: Applied when pagination is silent. At or above continue_at the page continues; at or below new_document_at it starts a new document. In between is unknown: the page starts its own document and is flagged for review, so nothing is copied onto it on no evidence.

open_until_signature.comment: A document whose first page is one of these page types stays open through pages the signals cannot decide. It closes after the page carrying a signature, before a page the signals or pagination call a new document, and before the next encounter: a page whose own date of service differs from the note's AND that carries one of encounter_headers (a section header from section_header_canon.json). The next encounter closes the note even when printed pagination continues, because an EMR printout paginates several visits as one job (53688890: 'page 1 of 17' across five office visits). A differing date alone does not close it: continuation pages carry stray old dates (a 2017 problem-list date inside a 2025 note) whose only label is 'Date'. Page type names from page_taxonomy.json.

progress_note_envelope.comment: A document of min_pages or more that opens like a progress note and closes with a signature is one progress note: imaging_final sets every page's Final page type to Progress Note and moves the page's own page type into the sub-type (Laboratory Data -> Progress Note / Laboratory Data). It opens like a progress note when its first page's Extracted page type is in opening_page_types, or the first page carries a section header (a section_header_canon.json name) from opening_headers or open_until_signature.encounter_headers. It closes with a signature when its last page is signed (a signed page always ends its document).

default_final_dos.comment: A document whose first page's page type or sub-type is listed here is not a visit: its Final DOS is DOS_DEFAULT_DATE (dos_canon.json, 2022-02-02) on every page, whatever dates its pages carry. Each page's Extracted DOS is untouched. Names are page_taxonomy.json page types / sub-types, matched without case.
